name: Accelerating Sparse Deep Neural Networks
problem: Sparsity research mostly targets high sparsity levels that no shipping matrix-math unit supports, so it produces compression without speedup.
mechanism: Documents and designs the NVIDIA Ampere Sparse Tensor Core: a 2:4 semi-structured sparsity pattern (exactly 2 zeros in every group of 4 consecutive weights along the K dimension) so the hardware can drop half of every MAC while keeping a dense, regular memory layout - the metadata and pruning overhead is paid at training time instead of at inference time. Ships a training workflow (magnitude pruning plus fine-tuning to recover the accuracy lost to the constraint) that produces networks that satisfy the 2:4 requirement while matching unpruned accuracy.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): the 2:4 (50%) sparsity pattern 'leads to TWICE THE MATH THROUGHPUT of dense matrix units' on Sparse Tensor Cores. That is a hardware claim, not a model claim, and it is the number that made 2:4 the default structured-sparsity pattern. COMPRESSION RATIO: 2x (50% of weights stored, zero-valued). QUALITY COST: the training workflow maintains accuracy on 'a wide range of common tasks and model architectures' - pruning to 2:4 is not free, the cost is paid in fine-tuning, which is why this became the pattern of choice for inference-side sparsity.
